description: Run each SLSQP restart for only PROBE_ITER=50 iterations, and continue to MAX_ITER only those whose probe radius sum is at or above the 75th percentile of probes seen so far, so more of the time budget goes to promising basins.
In the second half of the time budget, half of the SLSQP restarts start from the best centres found so far with Gaussian jitter (sd 0.03), and the rest stay uniform random.
Seed half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts from a randomly rotated, scaled hexagonal lattice of 32 points centred in the square (with the usual 0.03 noise), instead of uniform sampling.

Guided restarts in the second half of the budget use a crossover of the best and previous-best packings (left part of one, right part of the other along a random vertical or horizontal cut, count fixed to n) as the SLSQP start instead of the best packing alone.

Replace the first SLSQP stage with an analytic-gradient quadratic penalty on overlaps and boundary violations, minimised by L-BFGS-B while the penalty weight rises from 10 to 1e5, then polish with the existing SLSQP.
Give SLSQP analytic gradients for the objective and for the full constraint vector (pair distances, boundary terms, radii), so each restart runs faster and more restarts fit in the time budget.

Replace the uniform random initial centres of the non-guided SLSQP restarts with a jittered 6x6 grid (32 of 36 lattice points chosen at random, plus small uniform jitter), leaving guided restarts unchanged.

Basin-hopping perturbation of the best packing, as specified, is already what the incumbent's guided restarts do (Gaussian jitter of sd 0.03 on the best centres, re-run SLSQP, keep only if the radius sum improves), so this idea would not add a new change.
Switch to local perturbation of the best packing after 40% of the time budget (instead of 50%), with every later restart perturbing the best instead of a coin flip at 50%.

After each repair, greedily grow every circle's radius (random order from the seed rng) to the largest value allowed by the walls and its neighbours, repeating until no radius grows by more than 1e-12, to recover radius lost to the conservative repair.
With probability 0.5 per restart (even n only), first solve a 180-degree point-symmetric half-size SLSQP problem, then start a full unconstrained SLSQP run from its output.

Add a gravity pull term lam * sum_i ||c_i - (0.5, 0.5)||^2 to each SLSQP restart's objective, with lam starting at 0.05 and decaying linearly to zero over the iterations (updated via the SLSQP callback), so the final objective is the true sum of radii.
Restrict SLSQP's pairwise non-overlap constraints to pairs whose starting centres are within 0.25 (about 2.5 times the typical final radius), so each restart uses fewer constraints and runs faster.
Over-provision each restart by solving for n+2 circles, drop the two smallest after repair, re-optimise the remaining n with a second SLSQP, and keep the best-of-restarts logic unchanged.

Anneal a random clearance margin delta (0.01 to 0.03) to zero over three sequential SLSQP stages inside _solve_once, so intermediate packings keep clearance and the final unconstrained stage moves less.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the existing _repair step still runs on every candidate, so the packings stay valid.

No bug makes the result meaningless. _destroy copies c and r before changing them. If the disc contains no centres, idx is empty and the start is simply left as it was. Re-placed centres are clipped to [0,1] and given radius 0.01, which is a sensible start for SLSQP. The call _destroy(*best, rng) only works if best has exactly two items (c, r). The job finished with a score, so it does.

Behaviour change to note: guided restarts used to be the incumbent's best centres plus Gaussian noise (sd 0.03) with radii reset to INIT_RADIUS. Now they keep the best radii and re-place only the circles inside a random disc. This is a real change to the search method, not a bug.

The numbers support the reported z. The candidate's sum of radii is 0.0058 lower (2.9307 vs 2.9365). With noise sd 0.0034 and one run on each side, z = -0.0058 / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) = -1.21. The harness value of -1.187 fits once the 4-decimal rounding of the inputs is allowed for (the range is about -1.19 to -1.23).

The evidence is weak: one run against one run, |z| about 1.2. The candidate looks somewhat worse, but this is not conclusive. Rejecting is reasonable, and no replicate is needed unless large-neighbourhood search is a priority idea.

description: After the first half of the budget, the guided restarts replace the global jitter of the incumbent with a destroy-and-repair move: a random disc (centre uniform in the square, radius uniform in [0.2, 0.4]) has its circles re-placed uniformly inside it with radius 0.01, then SLSQP runs on all circles and the existing keep-if-better check applies.

Seed each guided restart from the best 31-circle packing (found in the first 15% of the budget) plus one circle inserted at the grid point with the most clearance, with radius 0.01, instead of from the best 32-circle packing.

After the random-restart phase, polish the top K=3 distinct repaired packings each with one SLSQP run (MAX_ITER 1000, ftol 1e-12) started from its own configuration, repair the results, and return the packing with the largest sum of radii.

Add a radius-continuation restart: with probability 0.5 per non-guided restart, bisect a common radius rho in [0.05, 0.2] (6 steps, SLSQP maximising the minimum clearance) and start the sum-of-radii SLSQP from the feasible centres with radii set to rho.

Replace the uniform random initial centres of the non-guided restarts with blocks of a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3, digit permutations and start index drawn from the seed rng, mapped to [0.05, 0.95]^2), so successive restarts cover the square more evenly; radii init and the rest of the loop are unchanged.

Replace the random restarts with successive halving: pools of 16 random starts run SLSQP in rounds of doubling iteration budgets (40, 80, 160, 320), keeping the top half by repaired radius sum each round, and the best packing across all pools is returned; this replaces the guided restarts of the incumbent.

Replace the guided-restart logic with a population of the best 8 repaired packings: each new SLSQP start perturbs a randomly chosen member, and the result replaces the worst member if its radius sum is higher.

Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, first maximise the minimum pairwise slack of the centres with all radii fixed equal (SLSQP with a slack variable t), then start the free stage from those centres so the sum-of-radii optimisation begins from a well-spread layout.

issues: Integrity: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and no use of test labels. The new _lsg_init draws all its randomness from the seeded rng, and the result still goes through SLSQP and the existing repair step, so the validity check is not bypassed.

Bugs: none that make the result meaningless. Adding eye to dist avoids division by zero on the diagonal, and the (n,2) boolean mask on v is valid. Radii from _lsg_init can end up slightly larger than the wall gap or slightly overlapping after the push step. That is harmless because they are only a starting point for SLSQP and the repair step.
Side effect: the extra rng.random() call shifts the random stream compared with the incumbent. This is not a problem, but it means per-seed results cannot be compared one to one.
Cost: 300 steps of O(n^2) work with n=32 is cheap, so there is no meaningful risk of going over the time limit.

Numbers: candidate -2.9365 vs incumbent -2.9365, one run each. The difference is 0, so z = 0/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) = 0, which matches the harness. The reject decision is consistent because there is no evidence of a gain, and the change adds about 20 lines of code.
The incumbent mean comes from a single run and is already close to the best published value of about 2.9370, so there is little room left to show a gain at this noise level.

description: Add a Lubachevsky-Stillinger style soft-disk growth initialiser (300 steps, seeded velocities) used for about a third of non-guided SLSQP restarts, with its centres and radii passed to SLSQP as the start.

Replace the independent restarts with a single Metropolis chain: each step re-initialises 3 to 5 random circles, re-optimises with SLSQP, repairs, and accepts worse packings with probability exp(delta/T), where T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 0.0001 over the budget.
Replace the SLSQP local solve with a log-barrier method (L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, mu from 1e-2 divided by 5 over 8 stages), keeping the existing random restarts and repair.

Replace the guided restarts with a memetic phase: the first 40% of the budget is random SLSQP restarts that seed a top-8 population, and the last 60% makes Gaussian-perturbed SLSQP offspring of a random elite, with a shared per-run sigma adapted by a 1/5th-style success rule.

In the second half of the budget, half of the iterations re-optimise a random third of the best packing's circles (the largest-radius half plus a random sample of the rest) with SLSQP while the other circles stay frozen, accepting the result only if the repaired radius sum improves.
Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, run an equal-radius SLSQP stage (shared radius R maximised over the centres) and start the free-radius stage from its centres with every radius set to R.

After the random-restart loop, run a compass pattern search on the best packing's centres (random circle order, steps of +/-h in x and y, repair and accept only valid radius-sum improvements, halving h from 0.01 down to 1e-5), using the time budget up to 95% of time_limit.
Seed each non-guided SLSQP restart from a random partial packing of half the circles, mirrored by a random one of the 8 square symmetries (with small jitter), instead of uniform random centres.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Guided restarts now start from 0.97 * best[1], where best[1] is the repaired, valid radii array of shape (n,). They also use a smaller perturbation sd (0.02 instead of 0.03). _repair still runs after every SLSQP call, so the final packing is still checked and shrunk if needed. The diff changes two things at once, so the result cannot be credited to either one alone.

The numbers match the provisional decision. The candidate loss is -2.937 against the incumbent's -2.9365, a difference of -0.0005 in the candidate's favour. With 1 run on each side and a noise sd of 0.0034, the sd of the difference is 0.0034*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.0048, which gives z ≈ 0.10. The harness's 0.107 most likely comes from unrounded values. This is well below any significance threshold, so rejecting is correct.

Both sides are a single run (n=1), so the comparison has very little power. The candidate's 2.937 is at the best published value (≈2.9370), but the incumbent is already at 2.9365, so that alone is not suspicious.

description: For guided restarts, start the radii at 0.97 times the incumbent radii and jitter the centres with scale 0.02 instead of resetting every radius to INIT_RADIUS.
Boundary-first initialisation: seed a random subset of non-guided SLSQP restarts with about 4*sqrt(n) circles placed along the four walls, the rest uniform in the interior.

After the random-restart loop, run up to 30 trust-region sequential LP steps (linprog/HiGHS) on the best repaired packing, accepting a step only if the true constraints hold and the radius sum grows, then repair and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent.
Key SLSQP ftol and iteration cap to the fraction of the budget used (1e-4/150, then 1e-6/200, then 1e-9/300 for guided restarts only in the final 20%), leaving the restart logic unchanged.

Stagnation-triggered abort of SLSQP: raise a private exception from a callback when the best feasible sum of radii stalls for 25 iterations, and return the last iterate to free time for more restarts.

After the random-restart loop, identify rattlers in the best packing, re-optimise the remaining circles with the same SLSQP model, reinsert each rattler at the largest empty spot found among 4000 random samples, repair, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves.

Initialise each non-guided SLSQP restart with Mitchell best-candidate sampling (20 seeded candidates per centre, keeping the one farthest from existing centres), leaving the guided branch, SLSQP settings and repair unchanged.
After the greedy pairwise repair, solve an LP over the radii with the centres fixed (HiGHS, all pairs, wall bounds), shrink by 1e-12 and clip, and keep whichever packing has the larger radius sum.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness is seeded.

LP repair is sound: all 496 pair constraints are kept, radii are bounded by wall distance, and subtracting 1e-8 per radius leaves 2e-8 of pair slack, which covers the HiGHS (~1e-9) and harness (1e-10) tolerances.

Crash risk: _valid allows zero tolerance, stricter than the harness's 1e-10. _repair output that touches exactly, with rounding error around 1e-17, is now discarded where the incumbent kept it. If every restart failed the check, solve would return None and crash. It did not happen in this run (-2.935), but a small tolerance or a fallback is advisable.
Recomputed z = -(0.0015)/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) = -0.312, against -0.300 from the harness. The gap is probably rounding and does not change the decision.
The candidate scored 0.0015 worse than the incumbent, well within one job's noise (sd 0.0034). Rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

description: The LP repair's HiGHS feasibility tolerance lets radii overlap by about 5e-9, so the fix shrinks LP radii by 1e-8 and accepts a candidate only if an exact overlap and wall check passes.
Scale the repaired packing outward about (0.5, 0.5) by a bisected factor t >= 1, capping radii at t*r_i, wall distance, and half the nearest-neighbour gap, and keep it only if the radius sum rises.

Replace the random-restart loop with a 4-replica ladder of SLSQP solves whose objective subtracts w times the squared overlap sum (w geometric from 1 to 100), each replica restarting from its own state plus noise, with Metropolis swaps between adjacent weights on repaired sums, returning the best repaired packing seen.
Replace the uniform random starts of half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts with a greedy largest-clearance constructive start on a 60x60 grid, using radii of 0.9 times the clearance.

Switch every remaining restart to a guided restart from the incumbent once three or more restarts have matched the best repaired sum to within 1e-4, keeping the existing time-based guided rule otherwise.

With probability 0.5 per non-guided restart, replace the uniform random starting centres with a Riesz s-energy minimiser (s drawn from [1, 8] by the seed rng, 100 L-BFGS-B iterations, with [0.05, 0.95] box bounds acting as the wall term) before the existing SLSQP stage.

Non-guided restarts first solve a packing in a random stretched box [0, a] x [0, 1] with a in [0.85, 1.15], rescale the x-centres by 1/a into the unit square, and use them as the start for the usual unit-square SLSQP solve.

For half of the non-guided restarts, first solve a size-class SLSQP stage with k in {2, 3} random classes sharing one radius each, then release to per-circle radii and run the usual full SLSQP solve before repair.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. _relocate keeps a move only if the radius sum improves, and every accepted packing goes through _repair, so the output stays valid. The run produced a score, so _repair is defined in the unchanged part of the file.

Timing risk: the deadline (95% of time_limit) is checked only at the start of each relocation step, and one step runs a 300-evaluation Nelder-Mead plus a 100-iteration SLSQP with 624 constraints. The 15 s gap to the 45 s hard limit should be enough, but the overrun is not bounded.

The result is odd. The main loop is unchanged and relocation can only raise the sum, yet the candidate (2.9281) scored 0.0084 below the incumbent (2.9365). That suggests the incumbent's single run (close to the best published value of 2.937) was lucky, or that the timing-dependent CPU-time loop varies between runs. A replicate run of the incumbent would help.

Both sides have only 1 run, so the evidence is weak. Recomputed z = (-2.9281 - (-2.9365)) / (0.0034*sqrt(2)) = 0.0084/0.00481 ≈ 1.75 in magnitude (candidate worse), which matches the harness's -1.735 up to rounding and sign convention. Reject is fine as a provisional decision.

description: After the random-restart loop, run up to 40 hole-targeted relocation moves on the best packing: remove a random circle, place it at the grid-plus-Nelder-Mead point with the largest clearance, re-optimise all radii with a short SLSQP on fixed centres, and keep the move only if the total radius sum rises.

For about a third of non-guided restarts, solve four random quarter-size groups of circles in their own unit-square quadrants (each group solved with the same SLSQP model, then scaled by 0.5 and offset), merge them, and use the merged packing as the start of the global SLSQP stage before repair.

For each non-guided SLSQP restart, a seed-driven coin flip (rng.random() < 0.5) chooses whether the initial radii are 0.12 instead of INIT_RADIUS=0.05, keeping the uniform random centres and the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

After each repaired restart, remove the smallest-radius circle, place it at the point of greatest clearance among 2000 seeded random samples (radius 0), run one SLSQP solve from that start, and keep the repaired result only if it beats the incumbent.

For half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts, seed the centres on 2 or 3 concentric square rings (inset from the walls, evenly spaced, circles split by perimeter with a seeded random phase and small jitter) instead of uniform random points.

After each repaired SLSQP restart, run 5 weighted (power-diagram) Lloyd iterations on the centres with radii fixed, repair, run a 100-iteration SLSQP polish from there, and keep the better of the two candidates.

Replace the guided restart's global centre jitter with heavy-tailed Levy-style jumps of 1 to 3 circles (weighted toward small radii), each moved to a uniform position or a Pareto-length step, and give moved circles the incumbent's minimum radius before the usual SLSQP and repair.

For half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts, seed the centres from a jittered hexagonal lattice with about n+k sites in the unit square (k uniform in 2..6, random orientation, spacing and offset), with random removal or fill to exactly n points, then keep the rest of the restart logic unchanged.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. The method is unchanged: SLSQP plus the existing repair step.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The `mu=mu` default argument captures each value correctly inside the loop. The penalty `max(0, gap)^2` can be differentiated. The last solve uses mu = 0, so it optimises the true objective under the exact constraints. `iu` comes from the enclosing scope, the same as in `cons`.
Minor: the code comment says 'geometric decay to 0', but the schedule is 0.05, 0.005, 0.0. That is two geometric steps and then a jump to 0. The comment is wrong, but this does not affect the result.

Risk, not a veto: each restart now runs SLSQP 3 times. That means fewer restarts. It also means a restart started just before the 80% time cutoff could run longer than before. Check that the time stays well under 45 s.

The numbers support rejecting the candidate. Its loss of -2.9081 is 0.0284 worse than the incumbent's -2.9365. With noise sd 0.0034 and 1 run on each side, se = 0.0034 × √2 ≈ 0.00481, which gives z ≈ -5.9. The harness reports -5.840, which is consistent once rounding is allowed for. The candidate is also well below the starting script's 2.9253.
Only 1 run was made on each side, but the gap is so large that a replicate is not needed to reject.

description: Each SLSQP restart becomes three chained solves, with the objective gaining a squared-gap pull mu * sum max(0, d_ij - r_i - r_j)^2 at mu = 0.05, 0.005, then 0 (exact constraints), while the constraints and repair stay unchanged.

After the random-restart loop, repeatedly remove k in {2..5} smallest-radius circles from the incumbent, reinsert each at the best of 3000 random candidates (largest free space, radius 0.01), re-solve with SLSQP, and keep the repaired result if its sum is larger, until 95% of the CPU budget is used.

For non-guided restarts with n > 20, half of them first solve a 20-circle boundary shell on an inset rectangle (random margin in [0.05, 0.15], random edge positions), then add the remaining circles at random interior positions and run a full SLSQP on all n circles before the usual repair.

Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, each restart draws fixed weights w_i in [0.6, 1.4] and solves a scale-only SLSQP (maximise s with radii s*w_i), then uses those centres and radii as the start of the existing free-radius stage.

After the random-restart loop, run up to 25 kicks that translate a random 3-to-6-circle contact cluster of the best packing by a random 0.05-0.15 vector, then re-solve with 100-iteration SLSQP and keep the result only if its radius sum improves.
For non-guided restarts, run SLSQP three times with a common radius cap (0.12, 0.2, then 0.5) warm-started from each other, then a final uncapped free-radius solve, before the usual repair.

With probability 0.3 per non-guided restart, solve a mirror-symmetric (x -> 1 - x) packing on reduced variables (m = n//2 free centres, mirrors, and one axis centre when n is odd, plus all radii), then unfold and run one unconstrained SLSQP polish on all 3n variables before the existing clip and repair.

Group guided restarts into cohorts of 4 that share a jitter amplitude drawn from {0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.2} via the seed rng, so each cohort starts from the incumbent centres with that Gaussian noise, keeping the 50/50 guided split and 80% time fraction.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. All randomness, including the new sd draw, comes from the rng built from the seed.

No result-breaking bug. On the first pass both snap and best are None, so the start is random. On the next pass snap is set to best because snap is None, which avoids indexing None. After that, snap is refreshed every 40 restarts and guided starts alternate with random ones. The _repair and clip steps still run, so the packing stays valid.

Behaviour change: guided restarts used to begin only after half the time budget, with probability 0.5. Now they begin after the first restart and happen on every even k, from a snapshot that can be out of date. The perturbation sd is drawn log-uniform from [0.005, 0.1] instead of being fixed at 0.03. This is a real change to the search, not just a tidy-up.

Recomputed z: the candidate's loss is 0.0020 worse (higher) than the incumbent's. The standard error with one run on each side is 0.0034*sqrt(2), about 0.00481. So z is about -0.416, with negative meaning the candidate is worse. This is close to the harness's -0.421; the gap is probably rounding in the displayed means. 'Reject' matches the sign.
The evidence is weak. With one run each, |z| < 0.5 cannot tell this edit apart from noise. Rejecting is reasonable, but the numbers do not show that the candidate is actually worse.

description: Run restarts in cohorts of 40 that alternate uniform random starts (odd) with incumbent-jittered starts (even), where each even restart's jitter sd is drawn log-uniformly from [0.005, 0.1] and each cohort's reference packing is the incumbent at the cohort start.

For half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts, start the centres from k=3 or 4 random cluster centres in [0.2, 0.8]^2 with each circle at a Gaussian offset (sd 0.12) from a randomly assigned cluster, clipped to [0.05, 0.95], keeping the initial radius and the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

Each SLSQP restart becomes a shrink-then-regrow homotopy: after the first free-radius solve, scale all radii by 0.9 and re-solve, then scale by 0.97 and re-solve, before the repair and selection steps, which are unchanged.

Lazy pairwise constraint generation: SLSQP starts with non-overlap constraints only for pairs whose start centres are within 2.5 times the start radius sum, then adds any violated pairs and re-solves from the last iterate for up to 5 rounds.

Guided restarts displace the incumbent centres along random low-frequency Laplacian eigenvectors (2nd to 6th smallest) of its contact graph, with the incumbent radii as the SLSQP start, instead of uniform Gaussian jitter.

Add a temporary repulsive Gaussian potential centred at a seed-drawn random point q in [0,1]^2 (weight 0.02, width 0.05) to the SLSQP objective of each non-guided restart for its first 30 iterations, then solve the remaining iterations on the true sum of radii.

Guided restarts splice two random elite packings (top 4 repaired, distinct by radius sum) along a random line through the square, then run the existing jitter, SLSQP and repair pipeline on the spliced centres.

For guided restarts, replace the isotropic centre jitter with a random shear A = I + 0.04*G applied about (0.5, 0.5), rescaled into [0.05, 0.95], and start SLSQP from the incumbent radii scaled by 0.95.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. A packing goes into the pool before the guided branch can read it, so the pool is never empty when guided is True. best is the top entry of the pool, so the largest exponent is 0: no overflow and the probabilities add to 1. The parent passed in is a centres array, the same kind of input as best[0] before. Every result still goes through clip and repair, so validity is unchanged.

Recomputed z = (2.9308 - 2.9365) / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) ≈ -1.19, assuming one run on each side and job sd 0.0034. This matches the harness value of -1.178 up to rounding of the values shown. The candidate is worse by about 0.0057, which is within noise, so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.

Side note, not a veto: guided restarts still happen only in the second half of the time and only half the time. Drawing parents from the pool with a softmax at T=0.01 may spread effort away from the best packing. One run is too few to tell whether that matters.

description: Guided restarts pick their parent by a categorical draw over up to 30 stored repaired packings, weighted by exp((sum - incumbent sum) / 0.01), instead of always using the incumbent.

Before the SLSQP hard-constraint solve, each restart runs three L-BFGS-B stages (beta = 20, 80, 320) maximising sum of radii plus the soft-min of all clearances (pair and wall) via log-sum-exp, with analytic gradients.

For guided restarts, with probability 0.5 swap the centres of a random pair of incumbent circles whose radii differ by at least 30 percent, then run SLSQP from that configuration with centre jitter 0.01 instead of 0.03.

Three-phase schedule: random restarts for the first 60% of the usable budget, then guided restarts from the incumbent with jitter halving every 10 restarts until 85%, then one 1000-iteration zero-jitter SLSQP solve from each of the top 3 distinct repaired packings.

After the random-restart loop, run up to 20 core-rotation kicks on the best packing (circles within 0.3 of (0.5, 0.5) rotated by a seeded angle in [-0.5, 0.5] rad), each followed by clip, repair and 100-iteration SLSQP, keeping the largest sum of radii.

In guided restarts, pick one incumbent contact pair (gap below 1e-6) at random and drop only that pair's non-overlap constraint from the SLSQP call, then repair and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent.

Replace the fixed half-budget guided switch with a UCB bandit over two restart arms (fresh random start vs. guided start from the incumbent), rewarding each arm by its mean improvement over the incumbent, with each arm pulled twice before UCB takes over.

Before each guided SLSQP restart, run 200 Monte Carlo moves on the incumbent centres (Gaussian steps with sd 0.01 times radius, accepted only if no overlap or wall violation results with radii fixed), then continue with the usual SLSQP and jitter.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The guided restarts now perturb the best centres with a noise sd that shrinks geometrically from 0.08 to 0.005 over the second half of the time budget, and start from 0.9 times the best radii instead of INIT_RADIUS. The packing is still clipped and repaired before validation, so outputs stay valid.

Recomputed z: the loss difference is (-2.9246) - (-2.9365) = +0.0119, so the candidate is worse. With noise sd 0.0034 and one run on each side, the standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(2) = 0.00481, giving z = -0.0119/0.00481 ≈ -2.47. This is consistent with the harness value of -2.461; the gap comes from the displayed values being rounded to 4 decimals.

This is weak evidence: there is only one candidate run and one incumbent run. Still, the candidate (2.9246) is below even the starting script (~2.9253). One possible cause: the initial sd of 0.08 is large, so the early guided restarts may throw away most of the incumbent's structure. Rejecting is reasonable.

description: Guided restarts use a centre jitter that decays geometrically from 0.08 to 0.005 over the guided phase, with radii started at 0.9 times the incumbent radii, and the guided-versus-random choice is unchanged.

Random-key GA over greedy grid-insertion orders (60x60 grid decode, tournament 3, uniform crossover, key sd 0.05, elitism 2), then polish the best decoded packing with _solve_once at zero jitter, which I am aborting rather than spending a slot on.

Split the random-restart loop across 4 seeded islands, each with a local elite of 3 and 5 restarts per round, where rounds after the first two draw starts from a random own-or-ring-neighbour elite with probability 0.5, and the best elite of each island migrates around the ring after every round.

Guided restarts move the smallest-radius incumbent circle to the circumcentre of the largest empty Delaunay triangle inside the square (ghost corner points keep the hull bounded) before the usual SLSQP solve.

Replace the non-guided SLSQP starts with a hard-disk NPT Monte Carlo compression (fixed diameter, geometrically rising pressure, single-disk and volume moves), then set half-gap radii and polish with the existing SLSQP, while guided restarts are unchanged.

For non-guided restarts, relax the uniform random centres and radii 0.05 with 400 steps of overlap-energy Langevin dynamics (temperature decaying geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-5, step 1e-3) before the existing SLSQP solve.
